items.summary: In every consequential field of human endeavour, whether in the boardroom, the courtroom, or on the trading floor, one resource has consistently separated those who prevail from those who do not. The resource is intelligence: information that has been processed, placed in context, and converted into a decision within the window in which that decision still counts. Military history makes the point plainly. The intelligence failures that determined the outcomes of wars were rarely failures of collection; the signals were usually present. The architect delivers a brilliant blueprint: a design that is elegant, compliant with all building codes, and visionary in its scope. The legal team ensures all contracts are sound and permits are in order. But without an engineer to translate those plans into structural realities, without a construction crew to pour the foundation and erect the steel, the blueprint remains just that: a brilliant but unrealized idea. items.title: The crisis after the flood in Assam villages: Lost livestock, missed crop, and wait for aid
items.summary: When the floodwaters rose around their home in Rajapul on July 19, Bandana Buragohain had no way of getting out on her own. The 70-year-old clung to the back of a man from her village as he waded into the current. At one point, the force of the water pushed him backwards. A couple of other boys came and helped carry her to a nearby house with a terrace, where around 30 others had already taken shelter. “I somehow managed to stay alive. I could have died,” she recalled. Rajapul, in the Nazira subdivision of Sivasagar district, was among the areas caught in the path of what several reports have described as one of Assam's worst localised floods since the 1950s. items.title: Hyderabad: Govt land auction beside Durgam Cheruvu sparks row over heritage rock site
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Telangana government’s call to auction 10.63 acres of prime real estate in Hyderabad’s IT corridor for a minimum of Rs 1,860 crore has triggered criticism as the plots lie right next to the Durgam Cheruvu lake. Critics have expressed concern that the land falls within the lake’s catchment area and is also close to heritage hillocks protected by the Hyderabad Urban Development Authority Zoning Regulations 1981. The e-auction of the two adjacent plots, part of the Raidurg Hyderabad Knowledge City, is scheduled for August 21 and 28, the Telangana State Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) has announced. The plots in survey no. 83/1 – 5.25 acres and 5.38 acres – fall under the Raidurg Panmaktha village of Serilingampally mandal. The TGIIC has set a minimum price of Rs 175 crore per acre for the auction. The Corporation also said that the site boundaries depicted in images in its auction brochure were only representative, and the exact land extent would be determined through a joint survey along with the successful bidder.
